kicker: The lantern is you; how far the agent goes depends on the power you give it.
summary: Give an agent just enough power; for anything you can’t undo, have it ask you first.

quiz.q: The agent has checked calendars and drafted the invite email. When should it stop and ask you?
options: No need to ask at all
quiz.explain: Checking calendars or drafting can be fixed; a sent email can’t be taken back.

autonomy.label: Levels of autonomy

scale.text: A 5-level scale made by AI Zen to make it easy to picture

autonomy.art: The stone lantern is you, the red spark is the agent. The higher its autonomy, the farther the agent strays from the lantern’s light.

levels.name: Answer
levels.does: You ask, it answers. You still do every step yourself.
levels.example: Example: asking how to write an Excel formula.

levels.name: Suggest
levels.does: It sketches a few paths; you pick one and walk it yourself.
levels.example: Example: proposing three meeting times for you to choose from.

levels.name: Acts with step-by-step approval
levels.does: At each step it asks “shall I go on?”, and acts only when you nod.
levels.example: Example: editing a price list line by line, waiting for you to approve.

levels.name: Works alone, reports at the end
levels.does: You hand over the whole job; it walks the whole path, then reports back.
levels.example: Example: reading 30 customer emails and summing them up in one report.

levels.name: Sets its own sub-goals
levels.does: You name only the big goal; it splits the work and opens new paths on its own.
levels.example: Example: “prepare the workshop” — it makes a task list and works through it.

autonomy.insight: The more autonomy, the farther the agent goes from your sight: handier, but it needs boundaries and careful checks.
autonomy.detail: Tip: pick the lowest level that gets the job done. The more important the task, the more the agent should ask you.

kinds.label: Kinds of agents

items.name: Chat assistant with tools
items.what: Chats like a chatbot, but can use tools on its own: search the web, read files, do math.
items.example: Ask “will it rain in Da Lat tomorrow?” and it searches the web, then answers.

items.name: Automated workflow
items.what: A workflow is a pre-drawn route: fixed steps that run exactly the same every time.
items.example: New order → send a thank-you email → log it in a spreadsheet.

items.name: Coding agent
items.what: A coding agent writes code, runs it, and fixes the errors it finds.
items.example: Describe an event sign-up page, and it builds a working website.

items.name: Computer-use agent
items.what: Computer-use and browser agents look at the screen, move the mouse, click and type like a person.
items.example: Open a browser, fill in a meeting-room booking form, compare flight prices.

items.name: Research agent
items.what: A research agent reads many sources, compares them, then writes a report that cites them.
items.example: Look into five competitors and sum them up in one comparison table.

items.name: Team of agents
items.what: Multi-agent: a lead agent splits the work among sub-agents, then gathers the results.
items.example: One agent finds the numbers, one writes, one checks for mistakes.

kinds.insight: A workflow follows a pre-drawn path; an agent chooses its own steps. Pick the kind that’s just enough for your job.
kinds.detail: For the same job every day, a workflow is cheaper and steadier; you only need an agent when the work takes thinking and adapting.

sim.label: Try handing off a task
sim.region: Simulation: an agent schedules a meeting and drafts a reminder email
sim.task: Schedule a team meeting and send a reminder email
plan: Find 30 minutes when everyone is free
sim.subject: 30-min team meeting · Thursday 2pm
body: Let’s meet for 30 minutes to lock in next month’s plan.
sim.note: There are two people named Minh in the contacts; I picked the first one.
sim.checkTitle: The agent stops and waits for you

stone.text: In Japanese tea gardens, a rope-tied stone set on the stepping path tells guests: please don’t go this way.

sim.editHint: Tap the recipient that needs fixing
sim.sentWrong: Sent, Minh at the partner company included. Once it’s gone, it can’t be taken back.
sim.sentRight: Sent to the right three people on the team. The meeting is set.
sim.insight: Let the agent check and draft on its own; but for sending, paying or deleting data, have it stop and ask you.
sim.detail: Those things are hard to undo. An agent can pick the wrong person or the wrong time; a few seconds of review saves you trouble.
